links.comparator_used: Same LLMs (GPT-4o and o1-mini) without RAG, relying on training knowledge alone
links.outcome: Adherence to Canadian radiology guidelines for incidental hepatobiliary findings (319 clinical cases)
links.effect: GPT-4o: 97.2% with RAG vs 81.7% without; o1-mini: 95.1% with RAG vs 79.3% without; RAG-enabled configurations outperformed non-RAG counterparts (P < .05). RAG outputs also had improved reading ease and lower grade level scores, though still at advanced comprehension levels.
links.tradeoff: Response times for RAG-enabled models increased slightly due to additional retrieval processing but remained clinically acceptable.
links.quote: Model performance differed significantly across groups, with RAG-enabled configurations outperforming their non-RAG counterparts (P < .05).
